Earlier this year, there were rumours that Apple would launch a brand-new health app, debuting alongside iOS 26.4. That plan was subsequently delayed, and although iOS 27 has been out for quite some time now, there is still no sign of this revamp.

With the new generation Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 set to debut next month, one cannot help but wonder: will these new features be unveiled alongside the new hardware?

Precedents

First, it is worth revisiting why these features are likely to launch in September. You might be thinking: "Shouldn't all software be released in June?" But the truth is there are precedents to draw upon.

watchOS 9's Low Power Mode, watchOS 11's sleep apnoea detection feature, and watchOS 26's hypertension notifications—all of these features did not require the latest hardware, yet were all announced in September.

Based on the above reasons, Apple is likely to wait until September to unveil its latest Health app upgrade, even if these features do not necessarily require a brand-new Apple Watch to function.

There Is Still Time

Prior to WWDC27, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman warned that the health app upgrade, internally codenamed "Project Mulberry," might not make an appearance at the WWDC keynote. His prediction proved to be correct:

Does this mean Project Mulberry will definitely debut at the September keynote? Not necessarily. However, given that numerous features have been announced in September in the past, and given that this project is already known to be running slightly later than WWDC, the odds of a fall debut look quite high—even if it ultimately may not launch officially until October with iOS 27.1.

Feature Recap

Due to the many variables involved, the rumours surrounding these features have been going back and forth. You may have heard one rumour that Apple would launch a standalone Health+ subscription service with video content provided by doctors. However, according to reports, that plan has been scaled back, and the related features will be integrated into the existing Health app experience.

That said, two things are already very clear: first, Apple will launch an AI health coach that provides health advice based on your Health app data; second, real-time guidance for workouts and other health-related tasks via the camera. Additionally, another key focus of this upgrade is a brand-new Health app design that makes data more clear at a glance.

Beyond this, all we can do is wait and see. Personally, I am very much looking forward to having a better way to organise and understand my own Apple Health data.
